summary: Retrospectively captured the initial foundational design and architecture documentation developed before formal run-history enforcement was introduced.
reason: Preserve the project's initial vision and architecture as an auditable repository record rather than relying on conversation history.
validation: Reviewed the documentation set for consistency around simulation authority, observer-dependent perception, seeded persistent generation, offline/local AI, and WALang boundaries.
decisions: The simulation is authoritative; local AI may interpret language and narrate results but cannot directly declare or mutate authoritative outcomes.
The simulation determines what exists, the renderer determines what can be shown, and Perception determines what the observing character notices.
World geography is seeded and persistent while player knowledge begins incomplete and expands through discovery.
Important spatial scenes are instantiated/rendered on demand rather than forcing detailed rendering for every location.
WALang represents player intent rather than outcomes and must remain model-independent.
notes: Retrospective entry. The timestamp records when this history entry was created, not the exact times of the earlier individual design discussions or commits.

summary: Established mandatory timestamped change logging with an append-only JSONL run history, repository policy, automated validator, CI enforcement, and documentation navigation updates.
reason: Ensure every future meaningful design, document, code, schema, asset, test, tooling, or configuration change is recorded with an auditable timestamped explanation.
validation: Policy and validator design reviewed for append-only history, required metadata, UTC timestamps, changed-path coverage, and pull-request enforcement. GitHub Actions execution will provide repository-level validation once the workflow is present on the branch.
decisions: Every meaningful logical project change must add a UTC timestamped RUN_HISTORY.jsonl entry in the same pull request/change set.
Failed experiments, reversions, and rejected consequential approaches are part of project history and should be logged.
CI should reject pull requests that modify meaningful repository paths without newly appended run-history entries covering those paths.

summary: Added the production master plan, 32 requirements, 12 delivery gates, 32 dependency-ordered work packages, integrated Clearwater slice, decision/risk register and resource/release governance.
reason: Translate the preserved full game vision into reviewable implementation work without substituting an underscoped prototype for the generational multi-era destination.
validation: Reviewed for consistency with the six original foundation documents and current user requests. Automated documentation/contract checks are prepared but not yet executed for this change at recording time. No game, model, device or human benchmark is claimed.
decisions: The first integrated region proves creative crossing, investigation and persistent development; it does not remove industrial or modern systems.
Gates require observed evidence, not merely written specifications.
Public release scope, final setting/title, pricing, hardware and shipping model remain explicit unresolved or unqualified decisions.

summary: Specified core module ownership and contracts plus character, NPC, health, ecology, economy, construction, law, institution, technology, generational and emergent-opportunity domains.
reason: Define the authoritative simulation, data flow, persistence, observer knowledge and full-domain integration boundaries needed before native implementation.
validation: Source review covered ownership, bounded failure behavior, state/knowledge separation, causal evidence, resource accounting, fidelity transitions and migration/replay limits. Runtime implementation and qualification remain unstarted; repository CI will check static contracts/navigation.
decisions: Gemma 4 E4B is the lead evaluation candidate; E2B and 12B are alternative device-tier candidates, not qualified shipping defaults.
llama.cpp is a replaceable runtime, not a commitment to Meta Llama weights.
Godot, an independent C++20 core and SQLite are working choices subject to feasibility tests.
Relevant world facts are committed before events depend on them; generated narration cannot create evidence or outcomes.
Exact replay is version/fidelity/retention scoped, while consequential world history persists.

summary: Added art/audio, accessibility/localization, authoring/research/balance, test scenarios, performance targets, diagnostics, release/support, licensing/provenance, architecture decisions and dated technical sources.
reason: Make content production, quality, observability, distribution and long-term maintenance first-class parts of the production design.
validation: Checked provider/project sources for Gemma, inference runtimes, Godot native integration, SQLite, Steam disclosures and the schema-validation dependency. Documented performance/quality numbers as proposed targets, not observed results. Local-link/scenario coverage checks are prepared for CI.
decisions: Data-only mod validation is distinct from arbitrary native-code trust.
Model, asset and project licensing require separate provenance and owner approvals.
Accessibility views receive the same permitted information as visual play.

summary: Added four strict JSON Schema contracts, a 12-operation parameter registry, authored baseline fixtures, positive/negative conformance tests, documentation/traceability validation and an architecture CI workflow.
reason: Provide an executable development contract seed and repeatable checks before the native simulator and language integration are built.
validation: Authored static checks for JSON/schema validity, operation parameters, outcome rejection, plan budgets, spending contradictions, event variants and save metadata. Tests are not yet run at this record; actual repository results will be recorded separately. These tests do not execute gameplay, inference or durable saves.
decisions: The executable seed supports ACTION and PLAN; future conceptual command families require typed schemas/handlers before execution.
All registered seed operations remain marked runtime-unimplemented.
Grammar/schema conformance is not semantic authority or proof of game correctness.

summary: Updated root/documentation navigation and added contributor/agent rules, PR template, machine-readable requirement traceability, implementation status and an honest validation report; preserved original history and foundation files.
reason: Leave a navigable, auditable developer handoff that distinguishes specifications, static tooling and unimplemented gameplay.
validation: Read the live foundation branch and PR metadata before preparing changes. Existing foundation/history retained. Automated path coverage and static checks will run after attaching the commit to the draft branch; no main merge or runtime qualification is claimed.
decisions: Extend the existing docs/foundation-architecture branch and draft PR #1 without merging main.
B-001 is the first bounded native implementation work package.
Every future meaningful change continues to require append-only UTC history and actual validation reporting.
